text:
With Josh Morrissey out for 14 games, Neal Pionk became Winnipeg's workhorse: more than 24 minutes a night, three games over 26, and almost 30 in an overtime loss to Dallas. He answered with 12 points in 18 games, already matching his total from 51 games last season.

The production is better than it looks, and the defense is worse than it looks. Winnipeg has scored 6.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, so his point total could have been higher. But the Jets get only 49% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more against him last season (bottom 8% of defensemen) while he faced top competition.

Morrissey returns tonight against New Jersey, which should take some of the load off. The question is whether Pionk's minutes drop toward 21 or 22, and whether he plays better for it. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he moves the puck well (65% of exits with possession). Our projection: about 38 points.
